manifest.name: dsh-crew
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin: run work as a small crew of role agents (product manager, researcher, architect, engineer, test engineer, code engineer, QA, code reviewer, security reviewer, doc reviewer) that talk through files on disk, with the PM as the only voice to the user.
manifest.author: Stuart Hu

scripts.test: node tools/verify-guard.mjs && node tools/verify-rule-guard-map.mjs && node tools/verify-jobs.mjs && node tools/verify-mount.mjs && node tools/verify-preset-install.mjs && bash qa/run-all.sh

bundle.text:
# dsh-crew bundle patch — mounts the two HOST-plane plugins.
# Applied when this package is listed in a dsh profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`
# (i.e. after `dsh plugin --profile tui add dsh-crew`).
#
# Rows are addressed by id, so your own cordis.patch.yml can override or
# disable any of them.
#
#   dsh-crew-core       the always-on PM prompt section, and the installer that
#                       copies the shipped `crew` agent preset into
#                       $DSH_HOME/.agent-presets (the only home of the preset
#                       on dsh 0.1.x)
#   dsh-crew-git-guard  blocks pushes, tag pushes, force pushes and package
#                       publishing, whoever asks for them
#   preset-crew         the same `crew` agent preset declared for dsh 0.2.x,
#                       which reads preset rows instead of a folder. The last
#                       block in this file; the guard that keeps the two
#                       generations from meeting lives in
#                       dsh-crew/host/crew-preset.js, this row's own plugin.
#
# The role TOOLS are not here. They live in the `crew` agent preset - declared
# at the end of this file for dsh 0.2.x, and written as
# preset/crew/agent.cordis.yml for dsh 0.1.x - because a role's allow/deny list
# is checked against the preset's tool set when a child starts. A role filter
# has to be set in BOTH lists until one generation is dropped; configure the PM
# here.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-crew-core
      name: 'dsh-crew/host/crew.js'
      # config:
      #   # Folder holding your own role markdown files. A file found here
      #   # replaces the one shipped in the package (same file name).
      #   rolesDir: '~/.dsh/crew/roles'
      #
      #   # Limits the PM must respect. It asks you before going over any of them.
      #   limits:
      #     liveAgents: 20      # crew agents awake at the same time
      #     reviewRounds: 3     # review rounds before the PM asks you to decide
      #
      #   # Set false to stop the plugin writing the `crew` preset into
      #   # $DSH_HOME/.agent-presets. A preset folder this plugin did not write
      #   # is never touched, whatever this says.
      #   installPreset: true
      #
      #   # Where the PM keeps one folder per job. The default is RELATIVE to the
      #   # folder the session runs in, which is the repository — so the job folder
      #   # sits inside the repository at `.dsh-crew/jobs`, and one default serves
      #   # every repository. It is still single-use: the PM keeps it out of `git
      #   # status` through the repository's own `info/exclude`, never stages it,
      #   # never commits it, and drops the whole folder when the job ends. Name an
      #   # absolute path (or one starting with `~/`) to put it elsewhere.
      #   # An unfinished job here is put in front of the PM at the start of every
      #   # session, so a crash can be picked up; set resumeNotice false to stop that.
      #   jobsDir: '.dsh-crew/jobs'
      #   resumeNotice: true

    - id: dsh-crew-git-guard
      name: 'dsh-crew/host/git-guard.js'
      # config:
      #   # Set false to turn the guard off completely (not recommended).
      #   enabled: true
      #
      #   # Trust the root agent (your own session, the PM): its git and
      #   # publishing commands pass straight through. Every crew role stays
      #   # guarded. Set false to guard the PM exactly like every child.
      #   trustRootAgent: true
      #
      #   # One-shot push approval file. YOU create it; the guard deletes it as
      #   # soon as one push uses it. Default: ~/.dsh/crew/push-ok
      #   approvalFile: '~/.dsh/crew/push-ok'

# ── the `crew` agent preset, for dsh 0.2.x ───────────────────────────────────
#
# On dsh <= 0.1.x the `crew` preset is a DIRECTORY: `preset/crew/`, which
# `dsh-crew-core` above copies into `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets/crew`, where that
# generation's `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets` registry finds it. That folder
# is the only home of the preset there, and this block does not touch it.
#
# dsh 0.2.x deleted that registry, and the folder with it. Its replacement says
# so in its own words: "the registry neither scans directories nor accepts
# preset paths". A preset is now a declarative row of
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset`, and a plugin ships one by inserting that row
# from its bundle patch — which is this file, applied when this package is in a
# profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`.
#
# So the same preset is written twice in this repository, in the two shapes the
# two generations read: `preset/crew/agent.cordis.yml` for 0.1.x, and the
# `plugins:` list below for 0.2.x. Neither can be derived from the other. The
# persona row takes `text` in 0.1.x and `prefix`/`suffix` in 0.2.x, and the
# package names drift between dsh releases — which is why the plugin's preset
# list has always been a copy of dsh's own `standard` list, re-copied by hand
# when dsh moves. A role filter has to be set in both lists until one
# generation is dropped.
#
# THE GUARD, and why it is NOT a `disabled:` line. A row's `disabled` is
# evaluated against the LOADER context, which cannot see the registry service —
# only a `!!js` expression inside a row's `config` is evaluated against that
# plugin's own context. So a `disabled: !!js ctx.get('agentPresets') ...` line
# here is evaluated where `agentPresets` does not resolve: the expression comes
# out true, the row is DISABLED, and dsh keeps a declaration whose activation
# fails "on the roster with its diagnostic" rather than failing the profile. That
# is why the symptom was "Crew is missing from the preset picker" and not an
# error — a silently off preset, on the one generation that has no other home for
# it. The check therefore lives in `host/crew-preset.js`, mounted as this row's
# own plugin, where `ctx.get('agentPresets')` resolves against the row's declared
# injections.
#
# What that check still does: register the declaration only when a registry is
# up AND it is not the old folder-scanning one. On dsh 0.1.x the plugin does
# nothing and the folder install above is the whole story; on a dsh neither
# branch recognises, the Crew preset is MISSING rather than the profile failing
# to compose — the right way round, because a preset that cannot be mounted must
# not make a profile un-composable.
#
# `plugins:` is dsh's own 0.2.x `standard` preset with TWO deviations, and only
# these two:
#
#   1. The delegation group offers the crew roles instead of every way to start
#      an agent — no `subagent`, no `subagent_fork`, no codex or claude-code
#      product, no `workflow`, no `ralph`. That is design rule 1, the flat crew:
#      only the PM starts agents, and a role that could start its own would put
#      that grandchild out of the PM's reach forever.
#   2. `tool-web` keeps `fetch: false`, which is what the 0.1.x list has always
#      set. Handing role agents web FETCH is a widening of what they may reach,
#      so it is not something to change silently inside a compatibility fix.
#      Whoever wants it flips this one line.
#
# When dsh updates its own `standard` preset this list does not follow by
# itself: re-copy it and redo those two deviations, exactly as
# `preset/crew/agent.cordis.yml` says of itself.
- insert:
    - id: preset-crew
      name: 'dsh-crew/host/crew-preset.js'
      config:
        id: crew
        order: 5
        name: Crew
        description: >-
          The standard coding agent plus the dsh-crew roles: a product manager
          that talks to you, and researcher, architect, engineer, QA, code
          reviewer, security reviewer and doc reviewer agents it starts. The
          only way to start an agent here is a crew role.
        plugins:
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              suffix: Your working directory is {{cwd}}.
              prefix: You are a coding agent powered by the {{model}} model.

          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536

          - id: tool-bash
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
            disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'

          - id: tool-pwsh
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
            disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'

          - id: tool-fs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'

          - id: tool-fs-search
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
            config:
              sampleOverCapGlobResults: false

          - id: tool-jobs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'

          - id: skill-filesystem
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'

          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'

          - id: command-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-goal'

          - id: tool-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'

          - id: planning
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              planMode: true
            config:
              - id: plan-mode
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'
                config:
                  section: |
                    You are in plan mode. Stay in plan mode until exit_plan_mode succeeds or the user switches the session mode. Imperative language to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.

                    Explore first. Use non-mutating reads, searches, static analysis, and checks to ground the plan in the actual repository. Do not edit or write files, change configuration, run formatters or code generation that rewrites tracked files, commit, or otherwise carry out the plan. Prefer existing functions and patterns over new machinery.

                    The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability. These plan-mode rules override any later tool description or guidance that suggests using mutation tools; those tools remain listed to keep the tool catalog unchanged. Do not use todo_write to track this planning phase: it tracks implementation after an approved plan, while the plan itself belongs in exit_plan_mode.

                    Resolve discoverable facts by inspection. Use ask_user_question only for user-owned choices or material ambiguity that inspection cannot answer. Do not ask the user where code lives or how current behavior works when you can find out.

                    Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria; group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema, and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making design decisions.

                    When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting with a # title. Make exit_plan_mode the only and final tool call in that assistant response: it presents the plan for approval, and implementation begins only in a later step after approval. Do not paste the final plan as a plain reply or ask "should I proceed?" through prose or ask_user_question. If review rejects it, incorporate the feedback and present again. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with implementation.

          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'

              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'

              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:
                  thresholdChars: 8192
                  headChars: 4096
                  tailChars: 1024

          - id: delegation
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              workflowEngine: true
            config:
              - id: tool-subagent-control
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'

              - id: tool-subagent-list-agents
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents'

              # The crew roles, and the ONLY way to start an agent in this
              # preset. (deviation 1 above: the generic `subagent`,
              # `subagent_fork`, codex, claude-code, `workflow` and `ralph` rows
              # of the shipped list are deliberately absent here.)
              #
              # This is the same row as in `preset/crew/agent.cordis.yml`, for
              # the other dsh generation, and the option names are the ones
              # documented in full there: `rolesDir`, `roleAllow`, `roleDeny`,
              # `roleModels`. A role filter has to be set in both files.
              - id: dsh-crew-roles
                name: 'dsh-crew/host/roles-preset.js'
                # config:
                #   rolesDir: '~/.dsh/crew/roles'
                #   roleAllow: { code_reviewer: ['read', 'glob', 'grep'] }
                #   roleDeny: { engineer: ['crew_researcher', 'crew_architect', 'crew_engineer', 'crew_test_engineer', 'crew_code_engineer', 'crew_qa', 'crew_code_reviewer', 'crew_security_reviewer', 'crew_doc_reviewer'] }
                #   roleModels: { engineer: { provider: '', model: '' } }

          - id: tool-ask-user
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'

          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: true

          # (deviation 2 above: `fetch` is false here, where the shipped
          # `standard` list has true. The `web` service and its search provider
          # stay in the host composition; only the model-facing tool is
          # per-preset.)
          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              fetch: false
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000

          - id: present
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-present'

          - id: tool-plugin-manager
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-manager/tools'
            disabled: true

readme.text:
> **Version 0.13.0.**

dsh-crew is a plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh). It turns your dsh session into a
product manager (PM) that runs a crew of role agents: architect, engineer, test
engineer, code engineer, QA, code reviewer, security reviewer, doc reviewer, and
researcher.

You talk to the PM. The PM starts role agents for the work. A job's documents go in a
folder outside your project, so your project folder stays clean. They are read while the
job runs and are not kept after it. The files that do stay in your project are the five
that ship: the two READMEs, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `principles.md`.

Two lanes:

- `ask` — you want an answer. The PM answers. Nothing changes.
- `team` — you want a change. The PM runs the crew: one task per change, one round
  of QA, one round of each review, then a commit. Pushing and publishing still need
  your own yes, every time.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile tui add dsh-crew     # or --profile web
```

Restart dsh. Pick the **Crew** preset for a session.

1. Install the plugin (above).
2. Restart dsh.
3. Start a session on the **Crew** preset. Your session becomes the PM.
4. Ask a question, or ask for a change.

- The `dsh-crew-core` and `dsh-crew-git-guard` rows in your profile's
  `cordis.patch.yml`: roles folder, live-agent limit, review rounds, job folder,
  and the git guard.
- The `dsh-crew-roles` row: per-role tools and models. Which file holds it
  depends on your dsh. On dsh 0.1.x it is the plugin's copy of the preset at
  `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/crew/agent.cordis.yml`. On dsh 0.2.x — which reads
  preset rows and never that folder — it is the `preset-crew` row in the
  plugin's own `cordis.patch.yml`, and your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` can
  override it by that row id. Set a role filter in the file your dsh reads.
